Report Studio and Custom Views

Administrators build small HTML/Jinja/JavaScript views over curated read-only datasets in Report Studio; once published they appear under Custom Views for every signed-in user of that ADOM.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.plugin_studio audit.view
📍 Whereany device ADOM → Plugins → Custom Views / Report Studio; Global ADOM → Global → Plugins → Report Studio (URLs /plugins/, /plugins/gallery, /plugins/publishers)

What is it?#

Called Plugin Studio until 2026-10-22: that name now belongs to the Python studio (Script Library, console, data stores, connections, apps). Only the label changed — the URLs and the studio.plugin_studio key are the same.

Report Studio lets an administrator build a small page — a table, a set of KPI cards, a chart — from SATOM's cached fleet data, without changing SATOM's code. A plugin is a Jinja/HTML body with optional CSS and JavaScript, bound to one or more curated, read-only datasets. When it is published, every signed-in user finds it under Custom Views in the ADOM it was built in.

What does it do?#

  • Author a view: name, kind (view or widget), icon, datasets, optional Inputs, body, CSS and JavaScript.
  • Live preview the unsaved body in an isolated frame.
  • Start from an example — Browse examples offers dozens of ready-made views (fleet KPIs, device inventory, full server-policy table, traffic-log enabled policies, policies grouped by App ID, policies without a WAF profile, certificate coverage, pools by type, and more).
  • Lifecycle with gates: Draft → Testing → Published.
  • Inputs (filters the viewer fills in): Device, Select (fixed options), Text, Number, Date. Values reach the body as params.<name>.
  • Custom Views gallery: the published views of the current ADOM, each with its icon, kind and author.
  • Export / Import a plugin as a .satomplugin package to move it to another server without an update package. The import is two steps: the upload is checked and shown first (problems, warnings, what it creates and keeps, where it lands, who signed it), and nothing is written until you click Install.
  • Trusted publishers: register the public key of a SATOM Builder so the packages it signs read as signed.
  • One package check for every package, whichever way it arrives — see What the importer checks.
  • SATOM's light look in every view: the frame carries the theme tokens and a small class kit, and the editor lints the stylesheet — see Plugin CSS rules.
  • Code plugins: install a signed package that adds its own pages at /x/<slug>/.

Available datasets#

Key Contents
fleet_appliances The managed devices visible to the viewer: name, kind, firmware, host, port
server_policies Cached FortiWeb server policies (key columns)
server_policies_full Cached server policies with traffic log, WAF profile, monitor mode, comment and parsed App ID
server_pools Cached back-end pools (type, protocol)
web_protection_profiles Cached WAF profiles (signature and bot-mitigation references)
certificates Certificate Manager certificates (no key material)
audit_recent The 200 most recent audit-log rows; empty for viewers without audit.view
fleet_counts Device, policy and certificate totals
scheduled_actions Scheduled actions (name, action, next run)

You only tick datasets; you never write SQL. Datasets are evaluated for the person viewing the page: they return only rows of the devices visible to that viewer in the current ADOM (devices in maintenance stay hidden unless the viewer's profile may see them).

Requirements#

  • Cached data in SATOM for the datasets you use (for example, server policies are only present for appliances SATOM has harvested).

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open Custom Views and view a published plugin Signed in
Open Report Studio, create, edit, save, preview, change status, delete studio.plugin_studio
View a draft or testing plugin's page or frame (including the editor's live preview) studio.plugin_studio
Export, import, and enable/disable/remove a code plugin studio.plugin_studio
Open Trusted publishers, add, enable and disable a publisher studio.plugin_studio
Open a loaded code plugin's pages (/x/<slug>/) Signed in (the plugin may check more)

studio.plugin_studio is admin-only (only the seeded admin profile has it). Users without it get 403 on the Report Studio pages.

Every plugin action — viewing a page or its frame, editing, saving, changing status, checking status and deleting — works only on plugins of the ADOM you are in; a plugin of another ADOM cannot be reached by its address.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: plugins are reachable only within their own ADOM, datasets return only the viewer's visible devices (audit_recent needs audit.view), the frame no longer loads images from https: addresses, and draft/testing previews and the menu entries follow studio.plugin_studio instead of full administrator capability.

The Report Studio menu entry — under Plugins in every ADOM (in the Global ADOM: Global → Plugins, right below Automation; until 2026-10-23 it was under Administrator → Studio there) — is shown exactly to holders of studio.plugin_studio, the key the pages check. Custom Views is not offered in the Global ADOM.

How to use#

Create a view#

  1. Go to Plugins → Report Studio (any device ADOM) and click New view. The view is stamped with the ADOM you are in.
  2. Optional: click Browse examples and insert one.
  3. Fill in Name, Kind and Icon (a Bootstrap icon name such as bi-puzzle).
  4. Tick the Datasets (read-only) the body needs.
  5. Optional: under Inputs, click Add input and define Name, Label, Type, Default, Options (for Select, one per line as value|Label) and required.
  6. Write the Body (Jinja / HTML). Datasets are available as data.<key>.rows (and directly as <key>); inputs as params.<name>.
  7. Optional: add CSS and JavaScript. In JavaScript the data is available as window.pluginData and the inputs as window.pluginParams.
  8. Click Live preview to render the unsaved body in the Sandboxed preview frame.
  9. Click Save.

Publish it#

  1. In Lifecycle, click Promote to Testing and check the preview.
  2. Click Promote to Published. SATOM renders the saved body once more; if it has a render error, publishing is refused.
  3. The view now appears under Plugins → Custom Views for everyone in that ADOM.

To withdraw a view, click Disable in the Report Studio list (it returns to draft) or Back to Draft / Back to Testing in the editor.

Move a plugin to another server (export / import)#

  1. In the Report Studio list, click the download icon on the plugin's row. SATOM downloads <slug>-<version>.satomplugin (unsigned).
  2. On the other server, open Report Studio, choose the file under Import plugin and click Import. Tick Allow downgrade first to install an older version over a newer one.
  3. The Import plugin page opens: Check what this package does before it is installed. Nothing has been written yet. Review it (see The import page).
  4. Click Install, or Cancel to delete the upload.
  5. A signed package lands in Testing, an unsigned one in Draft. If a plugin with the same slug exists in this ADOM it is updated in place; an older version is refused unless Allow downgrade is ticked.
  6. Promote it as usual. Updating a published view keeps it published only if the new body still renders; otherwise it goes back to Testing.

The import page#

Every import — Report Studio's Import plugin and Plugin Studio's Import app package — goes through this page.

Part What it shows
Header Name, slug and version; Kind (View, Widget, App or Code plugin); Signed by (Vision EBC, a trusted publisher's label, or unsigned); Lands in (draft or testing); Rules applied (import or builder, see the policies)
Problems Each problem as <where> — <message>. This package cannot be installed until its author fixes these problems. Install is disabled while there is one
Warnings Shown, never a refusal
What the import does Creates (for example connection ddi, data store hosts (12 rows), script check-host v1 (published, for admins)) and Keeps as they are on this server (an existing connection, data store, script or API version, and an installed app whose draft is replaced while its published version and access stay)
Secrets for the new connections One password box per connection the import creates that needs a password or token (see below)

Secrets. A package never carries secrets. Type the password or token of each new connection in its box; it is stored on this server only (the vault, or encrypted in the database), like any connection secret, and never written to the audit log. A connection that already exists keeps its own secret. Leave a box empty to set it later in Plugin Studio → Connections: until then the app shows the problem connection … has no secret yet and cannot be published.

The upload waits on the server, never in your browser session, only for the person who uploaded it: The upload waits here for one hour, then it is deleted. Install and Cancel delete it too — one confirmation per upload, whatever its outcome.

Install an app plugin (Plugin Studio)#

A package of kind app is a Plugin Studio app with what it needs: its data stores (the app's variables, with their rows), its HTTP connections without secrets, their API Catalog versions, its design images and the Script Library scripts its Run a script steps use.

  1. Open Plugin Studio → Apps, tick Allow downgrade if needed, click Import app package and choose the file (the Report Studio import accepts it too). The import page opens.
  2. Check Problems and What the import does, type the secrets of the new connections, and click Install.
  3. SATOM creates what is missing — API versions (published), connections, data stores (with their seed rows, at most 500), scripts (published as version 1, for administrators) — and the app's draft. An existing data store keeps its rows (columns the package adds are appended), an existing connection or script is never changed, and an installed app keeps its published version and access list.
  4. The app's editor opens with a message listing what was created and kept and what is left To do. Review the variables in the data stores, test the draft and Publish.

spo-fortiweb (new FortiWeb server policy with DDI reservation, certificate, capacity-based FortiWeb choice and rollback) is installed this way.

Scripts in app packages#

Export app package also writes the published version (files and settings) of every Script Library script the app's Run a script steps use, and the HTTP connections those scripts call. Credential values never travel. A script that is not published is not exported; on a server that does not have it, the import reports the Run a script step as a diagram problem.

A packaged script must:

  • run with network None (no outbound network);
  • declare no credentials — it reaches an API only through its declared connections;
  • not use secret or tcp from the SDK (satom_script / satom_sdk) in any spelling — an import, an attribute, a bare name, getattr(…, "tcp") — and not use from satom_script import *;
  • not pass write=True (any write= other than False) in any call;
  • have no database fields (lookup, lookup_multi, dataset): they query this server's database;
  • declare only HTTP connections that exist on the server or come in the same package;
  • have main.py as its entry, and every .py file must compile.

Comments and strings never count. On import a missing script is created and published as version 1 for administrators (an administrator widens the audience); a script that already exists is kept, with a warning when its published files differ from the package's.

Install a code plugin#

  1. Under Import plugin, choose a code plugin package signed by Vision EBC and click Import, then Install on the import page.
  2. The Code plugins card lists it as restart required. Run satom execute restart-all on the server.
  3. After the restart the card shows loaded and an Open button to /x/<slug>/.
  4. Disable / Enable and Remove also take effect at the next restart.

Manage trusted publishers#

A trusted publisher is an Ed25519 public key whose signature an import trusts besides the built-in Vision EBC key — typically the publisher key of your SATOM Builder.

  1. Open Trusted publishers: the button on the Import plugin card of Report Studio, next to Import app package in Plugin Studio → Apps, or in the header of the import page (URL /plugins/publishers).
  2. Under Add a publisher, type a Label (up to 80 characters, for example SATOM Builder, Lab) and paste the Public key (base64 of the raw 32-byte Ed25519 key). SATOM Builder shows it on its Publisher key page.
  3. Optional: under Limit to these ADOMs (none ticked: every ADOM), tick the ADOMs whose imports may trust this key.
  4. Click Add publisher. The list shows the label, the Key id (the SHA-256 of the raw key — the id plugin.sig names), the ADOMs (every ADOM when none was ticked), the State and who added it when.
  5. Disable a publisher to stop trusting it; Enable trusts it again. Publishers are never deleted from this page, so the audit trail keeps saying which key signed what.

What a publisher's signature does, and never does:

  • a view or widget it signed lands in testing (unsigned: draft);
  • every package it signs is checked with the stricter builder rules;
  • a publisher can never sign a code plugin: code installs only when Vision EBC signed it;
  • a disabled publisher is not trusted: its packages are refused, exactly like any key this server does not know.

The same key added twice is the same publisher (That key is already registered as “…”.). The Built-in keys card lists the Vision EBC key ids.

Use a custom view#

  1. Go to Plugins → Custom Views and click a card.
  2. If the view has inputs, fill them in the bar above the frame; Reset restores the defaults.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Name Display name; the address slug is derived from it once, at creation Yes Policies without a WAF profile
Kind view or widget Yes view
Icon Bootstrap icon class (max 32 characters) No bi-shield
Datasets One or more keys from the table above No server_policies_full
Inputs Viewer filters: Device, Select, Text, Number, Date No device input named dev
Body Jinja/HTML, rendered in a sandbox Yes {{ data.fleet_counts.rows[0].devices }}
CSS / JavaScript Inline style and script for the frame No —

What the importer checks#

Every rule a .satomplugin package must pass lives in one package check. The import page, the /api/v1/builder/* endpoints and the SATOM Builder all run that same check, so a rule cannot differ between them. A malformed package is reported as a problem, never as an error page. Each problem names where it is (app.graph, connections[ddi], style.css:12, …).

Two policies: import and builder#

Policy Applied to
import A package signed by Vision EBC; an unsigned package uploaded in the console
builder A package signed by a trusted publisher, however it arrives; an unsigned package sent through POST /api/v1/builder/import

The import page shows the policy under Rules applied. builder is the stricter one: what import only warns about, builder refuses.

Rules that refuse under both policies#

Rule What it requires
package.format The file is a readable satom.plugin/1 package: only the members plugin.json lists, each matching its sha256, sizes capped, and a signature (when there is one) by a key this server trusts.
package.min_satom min_satom is not newer than this server's version.
code.signature A code plugin is signed by Vision EBC; unsigned code is never installed and a publisher can never sign code.
app.definition app.json is well formed: the app id, the form, the actions, the diagram (an object of at most 512 KiB) and the design are valid -- what install would otherwise fail on.
app.template A package never replaces or creates a template (Plugin Studio > Examples, ex-*): app, data store, connection or script.
app.script_app A package never replaces a script app.
asset.name Every assets/* image matches its SHA-256 name.
asset.image Every assets/* member is a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image within the size and count limits.
store.definition A data store has a valid id and valid columns (at least one).
store.rows Every seed row fits the store's columns and the size limits.
connection.secret A connection never carries a secret (non-empty password, secret, token, api_key or client_secret).
connection.postgres A postgres connection never travels in an app package.
connection.definition A connection has a valid id, base URL and authentication.
connection.pin A connection is pinned to an API version that the package carries or that is published on this server.
api.definition An API version has a valid id, version and endpoint list.
api.empty An API version has at least one endpoint.
script.definition A packaged script has a valid id, files and settings (script_library limits); its entry is main.py.
script.syntax Every .py file of a packaged script compiles.
script.network A packaged script has no network (network absent or none).
script.credentials A packaged script declares no credentials.
script.sdk No source file uses secret or tcp from satom_script / satom_sdk (imports, attribute access and bare names).
script.write No call in a packaged script passes write=True.
script.db_fields A packaged script has no database fields (lookup, lookup_multi, dataset): they query this server's database.
script.connections A packaged script declares only HTTP connections that exist on this server or that the package creates.

Besides these, the importer itself refuses a code plugin that Vision EBC did not sign and a package whose min_satom is newer than this server, whatever the policy.

Rules that refuse under builder (warnings under import)#

Rule What it requires
code.builder A code plugin is refused, whoever signed it: custom logic is a script app.
view.template body.jinja parses in SATOM's plugin sandbox.
css.lint style.css passes the plugin CSS rules (its errors).
app.diagram The diagram has no problem (studio_flow.validate_graph), with the data stores, connections and scripts this server has plus those the package creates.
app.form_refs Every form.<field> the diagram reads is a field of the form.
app.design The design places existing fields, Output steps and images.
store.seed_limit A data store carries at most 500 seed rows (import installs the first 500).

Warnings only#

Rule What it says
view.datasets Datasets this server does not offer are dropped on import.
view.params Input parameters that are malformed or repeated are dropped on import.
css.warning style.css warnings of the plugin CSS rules.
app.downgrade A package older than the installed app needs Allow downgrade.
design.contrast Colour pairs of the design that are hard to read.
store.columns A column that exists here with another type keeps this server's type.
connection.pin_missing A connection pinned to an API version nobody has is created without a pin.
script.audience An installed script is for admins until an administrator changes it.
script.kept A script that exists here is kept as it is; a step runs its published version.

Rules that need no server state — secrets, PostgreSQL connections, empty API versions, connection definitions, data stores, scripts, images — are checked again by the install itself before the first write, so a refused package never leaves half its objects behind.

The rules pack#

SATOM hands out its package rules as a zip, the rules pack (GET /api/v1/builder/rules-pack): the package check and the modules it uses, copied byte for byte, plus rules.json with the SHA-256 of every file. The answer carries the zip's SHA-256 in the header X-Satom-Rules-Sha256. The same SATOM version always gives the same zip and hash. SATOM Builder runs the pack to check a package before sending it; SATOM checks the package again on validate, rehearse and import, so the pack can never accept something the server refuses.

Plugin CSS rules#

A view or widget renders in a sandboxed frame whose Content-Security-Policy is default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; font-src data:, so it cannot load SATOM's stylesheet or any file. So the frame brings SATOM's light look with it.

ℹ️Note

Changed on 2026-10-25: the frame dropped its dark default. A view written with light-on-dark colours keeps them, so light text now sits on a white page; the editor's contrast warnings point at exactly those lines. Replace them with the tokens. The built-in examples and the render-error card already use the light palette.

  • Tokens. Every --fw-* design token is set on :root, with the active theme from Settings → User Interface → Appearance (see Appearance) applied on top. Use var(--fw-text-primary), var(--fw-text-secondary), var(--fw-surface), var(--fw-surface-alt), var(--fw-border), var(--fw-accent), var(--fw-radius) … instead of fixed colours, and the view follows a customer's theme without a change.

The class kit — already styled, no CSS needed:

Class For
.fw-card with .fw-card-header, .fw-card-title, .fw-card-body, .fw-card-footer Cards
.fw-badge with .fw-badge-{primary,secondary,success,danger,warning,info} Badges and status colours
.fw-table (optionally inside .fw-table-wrapper) Tables
.btn-fw-{primary,secondary,outline,danger}, .btn-sm Buttons
.fw-alert with .fw-alert-{success,danger,warning,info} Alerts
.fw-muted Secondary text

Bare h1–h6, p, a, code, pre, table, inputs and buttons get SATOM typography.

  • Status colours come from the badge set, calibrated against white: success #15692A, warning #7A5700, danger #8B1C2A, neutral #3D4550, and #4C2A85 for a fifth category.
  • Images and fonts are data: URIs only. The frame uses --fw-font; Inter shows only where it is installed on the workstation, otherwise the system UI font applies.

Your stylesheet is added after the kit, so it can refine it. The editor lists the findings for the saved stylesheet under the CSS field, each as error or warning with its line.

Errors — a package checked under the builder policy is refused (under import they are warnings), and none of it works under the frame's policy anyway:

  • @import;
  • url(…) (or a string inside image-set(…)) whose target is not a data: URI;
  • expression(;
  • javascript:;
  • the behavior and -moz-binding properties;
  • position: fixed — an overlay pinned over the frame; use absolute or sticky;
  • @font-face whose src is anything but url(data:…) (local(…) included);
  • a stylesheet larger than 256 KiB.

Warnings — shown, never a refusal:

  • more than 20 !important;
  • color: set to a hex colour whose contrast against white is below 4.5:1 (translucent colours are composited over white first); a rule that also sets its own opaque background is not checked;
  • z-index above 1000;
  • a closing style tag in the stylesheet (the frame neutralises it, but it means HTML was pasted into the CSS).

Comments and the contents of quoted strings never trigger a rule (content: "@import" is fine), and CSS escapes are decoded first, so @\69mport is still @import.

Example#

🧪Example — Device count card

Tick fleet_counts, body: <h2>Fleet</h2><p>Devices: {{ data.fleet_counts.rows[0].devices }}</p>. Live preview shows the number; promote to Testing, then Published.

Result#

  • Saving, changing status and deleting are written to the audit log as plugin.save, plugin.status and plugin.delete; packages as plugin.import, plugin.export, studio.app.import (an app package) and plugin.code.install / .enable / .disable / .remove. An import entry records the version, the signer, who signed it (vision-ebc, publisher or none), the policy and whether it came from the console or the API — never a secret. Trusted publishers write plugin.publisher.add, .enable and .disable.
  • The Report Studio list shows, per plugin, the imported package version and whether it was signed or unsigned (authored here when it was never imported).
  • A published view is listed in Custom Views of its ADOM. Its address is /plugins/view/<slug>, and it opens only while you are in that ADOM.

Troubleshooting#

"A name is required."#

Possible causes - The Name field was empty on save.

"Move the view to “testing” and preview it before publishing."#

Possible causes - You tried to publish directly from draft.

Solution 1. Click Promote to Testing first, then Promote to Published.

"Cannot publish — the view still has a render error: …"#

Possible causes - The saved body raises an error with its default input values — an unknown variable (undefined values are errors), a typo in a dataset key, or a blocked operation.

Solution 1. Fix the body, Save, check Live preview, then publish again.

Verification - The preview shows the view instead of a red Plugin render error card.

"Import refused: …"#

The upload could not be read, or Install found a problem. After Install, the message lists up to eight of the problems, separated by ;.

Possible causes - The file is not a .satomplugin package (This is not a SATOM plugin package.), is larger than 10 MB (The file is larger than 10 MB.), or holds a file the manifest does not list. - A file does not match its sha256 (it was changed after the package was built). - The signature does not match (The signature does not match plugin.json -- the package was altered after it was signed.) — such a package is refused, never imported as unsigned. - The installed version is newer (… is installed and … is older (tick “Allow downgrade”)), or the slug belongs to another ADOM's plugin (the slug … belongs to a plugin of another ADOM). - Any rule of What the importer checks; the entries below cover the common ones.

Solution 1. Upload the package again and read Problems on the import page: each names where the problem is. 2. Fix the package where it was built (or ask its author), then import it again.

"Import refused: The package is signed by a key this server does not trust (…)."#

Possible causes - The package was signed by a SATOM Builder whose publisher key is not registered under Trusted publishers. - The publisher is registered but disabled, or limited to other ADOMs than the one you are importing in.

Solution 1. Open Trusted publishers and compare the key id in the message (its first 16 characters) with the list. 2. Add the publisher, Enable it, or add it again without an ADOM limit — see Manage trusted publishers.

Verification - The import page shows Signed by with the publisher's label and trusted publisher.

"That upload is no longer waiting (it expires after one hour). Upload the package again."#

Possible causes - More than one hour passed between the upload and Install. - The upload was already confirmed or cancelled (each upload is confirmed once), or it was uploaded by someone else.

Solution 1. Choose the file again under Import plugin or Import app package.

The Install button is disabled#

Possible causes - The import page lists Problems: This package cannot be installed until its author fixes these problems.

Solution 1. Fix each problem in the package, export or build it again, and upload the new file.

"connection … carries a secret (…): a package never holds one -- it is typed on the server that imports it"#

Possible causes - A connection in the package has a non-empty password, secret, token, api_key or client_secret. Packages exported by SATOM never do; a package edited by hand may.

Solution 1. Remove the value from the package's connection. 2. Import again and type the secret in Secrets for the new connections.

"… is a template (Plugin Studio > Examples): a package can never replace or create it"#

Possible causes - The package contains an app, data store, connection or script with the id of a Plugin Studio → Examples object (ex-*).

Solution 1. Give the object its own id in the package. To get the example itself, install it from Examples.

"connection … is a postgres connection: an app package carries HTTP connections only (external databases are this server's own connections)"#

Possible causes - The app uses a PostgreSQL connection. External databases are never moved in a package.

Solution 1. Remove the PostgreSQL connection from the package, create it on the importing server under Plugin Studio → Connections with the same id, then import again.

"API … has no endpoints: a version is published with its endpoints, so it cannot be empty"#

Solution 1. Add at least one endpoint to the API version in the package (or remove the version and pin the connection to one that exists here).

A packaged script is refused#

The messages name the script and, for code, the file and line:

Message Fix
script … asks for network …: a packaged script runs with no network Set the script's network to None and publish it again
script … declares credentials: a packaged script reaches an API only through its declared connections Remove the credentials; call the API through a declared HTTP connection
line N: secret() is not available to a packaged script (or tcp(), secret is not available …) Remove the use of secret / tcp
from satom_script import * is refused: import the names you use (inputs, result, log, connection) Import the names one by one
line N: write= is refused: a packaged script reads, it never writes through a connection Remove write= from the call
script … has database fields (…): they query this server's database and cannot travel in a package Replace the lookup / dataset fields with ordinary fields
script … declares connection …, which is neither an HTTP connection of the package nor of this server Use an HTTP connection that travels with the app or exists here

Fix the script in the Script Library, Publish it, and export the app again: the package carries the script's published version.

"a code plugin must be signed by Vision EBC: unsigned code is never installed and a publisher can never sign code"#

Possible causes - The code plugin is unsigned, or signed by a trusted publisher. A publisher's signature never makes code acceptable (a code plugin is installed only when Vision EBC signed it; a publisher's signature never makes code acceptable).

Solution 1. Build the custom logic as a script app instead.

"… needs SATOM … or newer (this server runs …)"#

Possible causes - The package's min_satom is newer than this server. A package built by SATOM Builder carries the version of the SATOM it was built for.

Solution 1. Update this server (Software update), or build the package for this server's version.

"connection … has no secret yet: set it in Plugin Studio › Connections"#

Possible causes - The app was imported and the secret box of a new connection was left empty. The app cannot be published until the secret is set.

Solution 1. Open Plugin Studio → Connections, open the connection and type its secret. 2. Publish the app again.

"Publisher refused: …"#

Possible causes - Paste the publisher's public key (base64). — the key box was empty. - The public key is not valid base64. - The public key must be the raw 32-byte Ed25519 key (N bytes given). — a PEM file or a key with a header was pasted. - The public key is not an Ed25519 key. - A label is required. / The label is longer than 80 characters. - This key is already trusted as a Vision EBC key.

Solution 1. Copy the public key from SATOM Builder's Publisher key page exactly as shown (base64 of the raw 32 bytes) and add it again.

A code plugin shows "error" in the Code plugins card#

Possible causes - A file in data/plugins/code/<slug>/ was changed or added after install (every start re-verifies the signature and each file), or the plugin raised an error while loading. The card shows the message; SATOM starts normally without that plugin.

Solution 1. Import the package again (same or newer version) and run satom execute restart-all.

A red "Plugin render error" card appears in the frame#

Possible causes - The body failed to render. The card shows the error type and message; the rest of the page keeps working.

The view is empty#

Possible causes - The dataset is empty on this installation, or its query failed (the dataset then carries an error note), or the inputs filtered everything out. - The viewer cannot see the devices the rows belong to (another ADOM, or in maintenance), or the view uses audit_recent and the viewer lacks audit.view.

"No published custom views in this ADOM yet."#

Possible causes - Views are ADOM-scoped. A view published in the FortiWeb ADOM is not listed in the FortiADC ADOM, and vice versa.

Advanced#

Advanced The sandbox
  • The body renders in Jinja's immutable sandbox with auto-escaping; attempts to call mutating methods or reach Python internals raise a security error.
  • Datasets are fixed, read-only queries (sensitive columns masked, at most 1,000 rows each). Input values never reach SQL — they only filter rows already loaded.
  • The output is served only inside an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> without allow-same-origin, with a restrictive Content-Security-Policy: the plugin's JavaScript cannot read SATOM's cookies, page or session and cannot call SATOM. Images are allowed only from data: URLs, so the plugin's code cannot send data out to an external host through image requests.
Advanced Plugin packages and code plugins
  • A .satomplugin file is a zip: plugin.json (manifest and the sha256 of every file), an optional plugin.sig (Ed25519 over plugin.json) and the files it lists — body.jinja, style.css, script.js for views and widgets, app.json and assets/<sha256>.<ext> images for apps, code/<entry>/… (text files only) for code plugins. Limits: 10 MB per package (also expanded), 2 MB per member, 200 members.
  • A code plugin's __init__.py defines a Flask blueprint bp; SATOM mounts it at /x/<slug>/ behind sign-in. It runs with SATOM's own privileges, which is why only packages signed by Vision EBC are installed.
  • The import page's upload is kept in data/plugin-import/ (owner-only files), bound to the uploader, and swept after one hour — never in the session cookie. The import page and POST /api/v1/builder/import end in the same install code.
  • The Vision EBC key is pinned in the code; trusted publishers are rows in the database. A database that cannot answer trusts no publisher (a refused import rather than a disabled key trusted).
  • Code plugins live in data/plugins/code/, so the HA standby receives them with the data sync and loads them at its own next restart.
Advanced What a published view exposes

A published view is offered to every signed-in user of its ADOM, but each viewer's datasets are filtered to the devices that viewer can see (ADOM and maintenance visibility), and audit_recent is empty for viewers without audit.view. Other datasets do not check the viewer's own permissions, so choose datasets for a published view with its whole audience in mind.
